# 什么是 CCBot（Common Crawl）？

- 原标题：What Is CCBot (Common Crawl)?
- 作者：Flavio Amiel Roborank 创始人
- 原文更新日期：2026-07-15
- 原文：https://roborank.io/glossary/ccbot/
- 栏目：[AI Search & GEO](https://roborank.io/ai-search/)
- 说明：中文全文翻译，后附英文原文。原文中的数据、观点、平台说明及推广内容均按原文保留，未经独立验证。

---

## 中文全文

CCBot 是 Common Crawl 运营的网络爬虫。Common Crawl 是一个非营利组织，发布免费、开放许可的网络档案。CCBot 使用用户代理标识 CCBot，将网页收集进 Common Crawl 的公开数据集；这一数据集曾被多个大语言模型用作训练数据，其中包括 OpenAI 的 GPT-3。

### 核心要点

- CCBot 的完整用户代理字符串是 `CCBot/2.0 (https://commoncrawl.org/faq/)`；可通过 robots.txt 中的 `User-agent: CCBot` / `Disallow: /` 规则屏蔽。
- Common Crawl 是基础性训练语料库：过滤后的 Common Crawl 数据集提供了 OpenAI 训练 GPT-3 所用 token 的约 60%。
- 由于档案公开，屏蔽 CCBot 可用一条指令限制一大类能够再次分发的 AI 训练用途，而不必逐家公司处理。
- Common Crawl 在 `index.commoncrawl.org/ccbot.json` 发布 CCBot 的真实 IP 范围，帮助运营者区分真实流量与伪造用户代理的请求。

### CCBot 如何运作

CCBot 是 Common Crawl 运行的 [AI 爬虫](https://roborank.io/glossary/ai-crawler/)。Common Crawl 是非营利组织，其目的就是维护一份免费、开放许可的网络快照，任何人都可下载和分析。搜索引擎抓取网页，是为了建立自己的私有索引；Common Crawl 抓取则是为了公开发布，定期提供原始页面数据档案，让研究人员、初创公司和 AI 实验室不必自己进行网络规模的抓取，就能获取内容。

CCBot 以用户代理字符串 `CCBot/2.0 (https://commoncrawl.org/faq/)` 表明身份，并遵守 robots.txt。网站若希望退出，只需加入两行：`User-agent: CCBot` 和 `Disallow: /`，未来的抓取就会跳过它。由于冒充者有时会借用 CCBot 的名称，Common Crawl 在 `index.commoncrawl.org/ccbot.json` 发布真实 IP 范围，使运营者可以通过反向 DNS 和 CIDR 验证真实流量，而不只是相信请求头。

CCBot 的独特之处不是爬虫本身，而是输出流向何处。Common Crawl 数据是大量公开构建的语言模型的原材料，因此一个被 CCBot 捕获的页面，可能复制进入许多下游训练集。这也是它受到的屏蔽关注远超其流量规模的原因：它是一条一对多的输送管道。

### CCBot 示例

Common Crawl 数据最具影响力、且有明确文献记录的用途，是 OpenAI 的 GPT-3。在 2020 年论文*《语言模型是少样本学习者》*中，OpenAI 详细披露了训练数据配比，其中经过过滤的 Common Crawl 远远占据最大份额：约 **4,100 亿个 token**，加权后约占**训练过程中所见 token 的 60%**。换句话说，GPT-3 学习语言所依赖的大部分材料，都来自 CCBot 所供应的管道。

仅这一事实，就改变了 robots.txt 决策的意义。发布者屏蔽 CCBot，不是在退出一个冷门研究项目，而是在拒绝为那类开启现代大语言模型时代、并持续支撑许多开源和商业模型的数据集贡献内容。这也解释了屏蔽率：2026 年 4 月，对美英排名前 100 的新闻网站进行的分析发现，CCBot 是**被屏蔽最多**的 AI 相关爬虫，**75%** 的网站禁止它，甚至高于 GPTBot 的 62%。

这一做法的局限同样重要。今天屏蔽 CCBot，并不能处理 Common Crawl 已经发布的档案；那些档案仍然公开存在，也已被镜像复制。它同样影响不了那些从未使用 Common Crawl 的爬虫。这是针对一个特别容易再次分发的语料库的精确工具，不是通用的 AI 关闭开关。要全面了解哪些指令管理哪些机器人，请参阅 [AI 机器人屏蔽](https://roborank.io/glossary/ai-bot-blocking/)；要用机器可读的方式说明内容使用偏好，请参阅 [llms.txt](https://roborank.io/glossary/llms-txt/)。

### 人们常犯的错误

人们以为屏蔽 CCBot，就能干净、彻底地让内容远离 AI。实际上，它只覆盖一部分，也只能影响未来，不能追溯过去。Common Crawl 档案已经公开发布、采用开放许可，并被复制进无数下游训练集。新增加的禁止规则可以阻止未来收集，却无法收回已经进入语料库的内容。而且，CCBot 只是其中一扇门，GPTBot、ClaudeBot、Google-Extended 等完全使用各自独立的标识抓取。我把屏蔽 CCBot 看作针对一个特定、特别容易再次分发的数据集的具体决定，而不是“禁止所有 AI”的总开关。网络并没有这样的总开关。

### 常见问题

#### 什么是 CCBot？

CCBot 是 Common Crawl 的网络爬虫。Common Crawl 是一个非营利组织，归档数十亿网页，并依据开放许可免费发布数据。这个档案是许多大语言模型训练数据集中的常见组成部分。

#### 如何屏蔽 CCBot？

在 robots.txt 中加入 `User-agent: CCBot`，后面跟上 `Disallow: /`。CCBot 文档说明它遵守 robots.txt 指令。屏蔽之后，可以阻止未来的页面被加入 Common Crawl 公开档案，但无法删除过去版本已经收集的内容。

#### 屏蔽 CCBot 会阻止所有 AI 用我的网站训练吗？

不会。它只阻止一个数据集。GPTBot、ClaudeBot、Google-Extended 等其他爬虫使用各自独立的用户代理标识收集训练数据，因此必须分别屏蔽。屏蔽 CCBot 只针对 Common Crawl 这个特定、公开再分发的语料库。

#### CCBot 和 GPTBot 是同一个东西吗？

不是。CCBot 属于非营利组织 Common Crawl，为公开共享的档案供数；GPTBot 属于 OpenAI，为其私有模型训练供数。两者运营者不同、标识不同、数据集也不同，只是都经常被希望退出 AI 训练的发布者屏蔽。

### 结论

CCBot 是 Common Crawl 免费网络档案背后的爬虫，该档案是 AI 中复用最广的训练语料之一，曾提供 GPT-3 大部分训练 token。管理它，是用一条指令针对一个特别公开的数据集作决策，不是一次性退出所有 AI 爬虫的办法；其他爬虫各自保留独立标识。

## 英文原文

CCBot is the web crawler operated by Common Crawl, a nonprofit that publishes a free, openly licensed archive of the web. Identified by the user-agent token CCBot, it gathers pages into Common Crawl’s public dataset, which has been used as training data for many large language models, including OpenAI’s GPT-3.

### Key Takeaways

- CCBot’s full user-agent string is `CCBot/2.0 (https://commoncrawl.org/faq/)`; it is blocked with a `User-agent: CCBot` / `Disallow: /` rule in robots.txt.
- Common Crawl is a foundational training corpus: the filtered Common Crawl dataset supplied about 60% of the tokens used to train OpenAI’s GPT-3.
- Because the archive is public, blocking CCBot restricts a huge, redistributable class of AI training use in a single directive rather than per-company.
- Common Crawl publishes CCBot’s authentic IP ranges at `index.commoncrawl.org/ccbot.json` so operators can distinguish real traffic from spoofed user agents.

### How CCBot Works

CCBot is the [AI crawler](https://roborank.io/glossary/ai-crawler/) run by Common Crawl, a nonprofit whose entire purpose is to maintain a free, openly licensed snapshot of the web that anyone can download and analyze. Where a search engine crawls to build its own private index, Common Crawl crawls to publish — releasing regular archives of raw page data that researchers, startups, and AI labs pull from without having to run their own web-scale crawl.

CCBot identifies itself with the user-agent string `CCBot/2.0 (https://commoncrawl.org/faq/)`, and it honors robots.txt. A site that wants out adds two lines — `User-agent: CCBot` and `Disallow: /` — and future crawls skip it. Because impostors sometimes borrow the CCBot name, Common Crawl publishes the crawler’s genuine IP ranges at `index.commoncrawl.org/ccbot.json`, letting an operator confirm real traffic by reverse-DNS and CIDR rather than trusting the header alone.

What makes CCBot distinctive is not the crawler but where its output goes. Common Crawl data is the raw material for a large share of publicly built language models, so a single page captured by CCBot can end up replicated across many downstream training sets. That is why CCBot draws blocking attention out of proportion to its traffic: it is a one-to-many pipe.

### Example of CCBot

The most consequential documented use of Common Crawl data is OpenAI’s GPT-3. In the 2020 paper *Language Models are Few-Shot Learners*, OpenAI details its training mixture, and a filtered version of Common Crawl is by far the largest ingredient: roughly **410 billion tokens**, weighted at about **60% of the tokens seen during training**. In other words, most of what GPT-3 learned language from came through the pipeline CCBot feeds.

That single fact reframes the robots.txt decision. When a publisher blocks CCBot, they are not opting out of an obscure research project — they are declining to contribute to the exact class of dataset that seeded the modern LLM era, and that continues to underpin many open and commercial models. It also explains the blocking numbers: an April 2026 analysis of the top 100 US and UK news sites found CCBot was the **most-blocked** AI-related crawler, disallowed by **75%** of them, ahead of even GPTBot at 62%.

The limit of the tactic is just as important. Blocking CCBot today does nothing about archives Common Crawl already released, which remain public and mirrored, and it does nothing about crawlers that never touched Common Crawl in the first place. It is a precise instrument for one uniquely redistributable corpus — not a general-purpose AI off switch. For the broader picture of which directives cover which bots, see [AI bot blocking](https://roborank.io/glossary/ai-bot-blocking/); to publish machine-readable guidance about how your content may be used, see [llms.txt](https://roborank.io/glossary/llms-txt/).

### The thing people get wrong

People assume blocking CCBot is a clean, complete way to keep their content out of AI. It is partial, and it is retroactive-proof only going forward. Common Crawl archives are already published, openly licensed, and mirrored in countless downstream training sets; a fresh disallow stops future capture but cannot recall what is already in the corpus. And CCBot is only one door — GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended and others crawl on their own tokens entirely. I treat blocking CCBot as one specific decision about one specific, unusually redistributable dataset, not as a master switch for "no AI." The web does not have a master switch.

### Frequently Asked Questions

#### What is CCBot?

CCBot is Common Crawl’s web crawler. Common Crawl is a nonprofit that archives billions of web pages and releases the data for free under an open license. That archive is a common ingredient in the training datasets behind many large language models.

#### How do I block CCBot?

Add `User-agent: CCBot` followed by `Disallow: /` to your robots.txt. CCBot documents that it respects robots.txt directives. Blocking it prevents future pages from being added to Common Crawl’s public archive, though it cannot remove content already captured in earlier releases.

#### Does blocking CCBot stop all AI training on my site?

No. It stops one dataset. Other crawlers such as GPTBot, ClaudeBot, and Google-Extended gather training data under their own separate user-agent tokens, so each must be blocked individually. Blocking CCBot only addresses Common Crawl’s specific, openly redistributed corpus.

#### Is CCBot the same as GPTBot?

No. CCBot belongs to the nonprofit Common Crawl and feeds a public, shared archive; GPTBot belongs to OpenAI and feeds its private model training. They are different operators, different tokens, and different datasets, even though both are frequently blocked by publishers who want out of AI training.

### The Bottom Line

CCBot is the crawler behind Common Crawl’s free web archive — one of the most widely reused training corpora in AI, having supplied the majority of GPT-3’s training tokens. Controlling it is a single-directive decision about a uniquely public dataset, not a way to opt out of every AI crawler at once; each of those keeps its own token.
